title: Cap. 6 Arg. 6 close: Obstacle and non-obstacle resolve into bare good pleasure—no promiscuous-grace decree
pass_a_gloss: Finally, lest we refer to the disparity of human wills the fact that these have obtained efficacious grace and have been converted, those have not obtained it and remain unconverted, he subjoins in the same place also these most worthy words: "When God, of human beings who are held in the same sins, converts some by preventing them, but sustains or permits others to proceed according to the order of things, a reason is not to be sought why he converts these and not those: for this depends on his simple will, just as from his simple will it proceeded that, when all things were made from nothing, certain things were made more worthy than others." Thus far Thomas. Therefore by the death of Christ no divine decree has been established concerning grace to be administered promiscuously to all human beings, with that quasi-law annexed, that particular persons become sharers of this grace, or not sharers, according as they are going to place an impediment, or not going to place one: but this very distinction between those who place and those who do not place an obstacle is to be resolved into the bare good pleasure of God, as into the first and radical cause.
pass_b_english: Finally—lest we pin on the disparity of human wills the fact that these obtained efficacious grace and were converted, while those did not and stay unconverted—he adds in the same place these weighty words: "When God, among people held in the same sins, converts some by going before them, but sustains or permits others to go on according to the order of things, we are not to ask why he converts these and not those. That hangs on his simple will—just as it was by his simple will that, when all things were made from nothing, some were made more worthy than others." So far Thomas. Christ's death, then, established no divine decree that grace should be administered promiscuously to all, with a kind of annexed law that particular persons share or do not share in that grace according as they will or will not raise an impediment. The very distinction between those who raise an obstacle and those who do not must be resolved into God's bare good pleasure as its first and radical cause.
source_text: Demum, ne ad disparitatem voluntatum humanarum referamus, quod hi gratiam efficacem obtinuerint & conversi sint, illi non obtinuerint & conversi maneant, subjungit ibidem & haec verba dignissima, Cum Deus hominum qui in eisdem peccatis detinentur, hos quidem praeveniens convertat, illos autem sustineat sive permittat secundum ordinem rerum procedere, non est ratio inquirenda quare hos convertat, & non illos: hoc enim ex simplici ejus voluntate dependet, sicut ex simplici ejus voluntate processit, quod, quum omnia fierent ex nihilo, quaedam facta sunt aliis digniora. Hactenus Thomas. Christi igitur morte non est stabilitum ullum decretum Divinum de gratia omnibus hominibus promiscue administranda, ea quasi lege annexa, ut singulares personae hujus gratiae participes fiant, aut non participes, prout impedimentum posituri sunt, aut non posituri: sed hoc ipsum discrimen inter ponentes & non ponentes obicem in merum Dei beneplacitum, tanquam in primam & radicalem causam, resolvendum est.
